summary.name: Nix
summary.one_liner: Nix is a package manager and build tool that provides reproducible development environments, declarative builds, and rollback-friendly system and software installs.
use_cases: set up a consistent development environment for a project
run the same build locally and in continuous integration
build cloud and virtual machine images declaratively
roll back to a previous software version
safely test experimental or bleeding-edge software
summary.what_it_does:
Nix builds packages only from explicitly declared dependencies, so a successful build shows all needed dependencies were specified. The same build specification can start a development environment, optionally with extra tools, without Docker or other virtualization. It can build Docker images, Amazon EC2, Google Cloud, Azure, VirtualBox and KVM images declaratively, and configure machines. Nix never overwrites files; it adds new versions at different paths, so older versions remain available for rollback. The page says development of Nix, the Nix packages collection and the NixOS Linux distribution happens on GitHub, where contributions are made through pull requests.</what_it_does>
<parameter name="pricing">open source
notable: Declarative builds where only explicitly declared dependencies are available
Rollback to earlier versions because nothing is overwritten
Same environment used for development, CI and deployment
Builds container and cloud/VM images without Dockerfiles
caveats: The page is a marketing overview and does not state pricing or detailed platform support
Page does not describe installation steps or a learning curve
